vocab.example: Her opening line really stuck with me.
He read the room and skipped the jokes.
With executives, lead with the result, not the process.
Don't say you're creative. Show rather than tell.
A little self-deprecating humour makes you more approachable.
That's basically what I do: I make complex data simple.
A good first line piques the listener's curiosity.
Bold claims need to be backed by real results.

tasks.title: Expressions in context
tasks.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form of an expression from the lesson.

items.text: Her talk was short, but one story really ___ with the audience.
If you'd ___ , you'd have noticed nobody wanted another slide.
When you pitch to investors, ___ the numbers, not the history.
His ___ joke about his terrible Arabic made everyone relax.
The headline was designed to ___ readers' curiosity.
These claims need to ___ data before we publish them.

tasks.title: Key word transformation
tasks.instructions: Complete the second sentence so it means the same as the first. Use the word in brackets. Use 2–5 words.

items.lead: Start with the result when you speak to the CEO. (LEAD)
items.text: When you speak to the CEO, ___ the result.

items.lead: He gave an example instead of describing himself. (RATHER)
The first line made them want to know more. (PIQUED)
Their success is supported by ten years of data. (BACKED)
items.text: Their success ___ ten years of data.

items.lead: She adapted her tone to the mood of the meeting. (ROOM)

tasks.title: Write three micro-stories
tasks.instructions: Write three micro-stories (60–80 words each). Each one ends with a summary line.

parts.label: 1 · Your work
parts.hint: A recent moment that shows what you do best

parts.label: 2 · A challenge
parts.hint: A time things went wrong, and what you did

parts.label: 3 · Outside work
parts.hint: Something that shows who you are as a person

tasks.title: One story, three audiences
tasks.instructions: Take your best micro-story from Task 3 and rewrite it for each audience.

parts.label: LinkedIn “About” section
parts.hint: The first two lines: the ones people see before “see more”

parts.label: A dinner with friends of friends
An interview panel
parts.hint: Linked clearly to what the role needs

tasks.title: Respond to the article
tasks.instructions: Write 150–180 words in answer to this question. Give your opinion, one example from your experience, and one counter-argument.

parts.label: The question
parts.hint: “Is telling stories about yourself at work authentic, or just a performance?”

checklist: Clear position in the first sentence

tasks.title: Record your best version
tasks.instructions: Record a video of your best micro-story. Review it honestly, then record it once more.
steps: Record your micro-story, without notes, in under 45 seconds.
Watch it with the sound off: what does your body language say?
Watch it with the sound on and check the list below.
Record your final version and send it to your trainer.
tasks.reflection: What did your body language say? What did you improve in the final version?
